annotations.text:
AsapLocal Business — provider app splash

Same 5s structure as the customer canvas, but built on the PROVIDER app's own tokens, which are not the customer app's. apps/provider/app/globals.css runs a cool slate scale (--background 222 47% 7%, --surface 222 40% 10%); apps/web runs warm espresso. Only the terracotta brand and Inter are shared, via packages/ui/tailwind.preset.js. The lockup mirrors AuthBrand — mark, wordmark, and 'Business' baseline-aligned beside it at text-sm/font-normal.

A · Lead feed — three real leads deal in, then resolve to the mark.

Why: a provider opens this app for one reason, and it is on screen in under two seconds. Card anatomy is the marketplace card from apps/provider/app/leads/page.tsx; the lead prices (£6.50 / £13.50 / £7.50) are what computeLeadPrice() actually returns for those budgets.
Tradeoff: it promises leads before it knows there are any. On an empty radar the splash writes a cheque the dashboard cannot cash.

B · Earnings — the money view: bars build, then the split resolves.

Why: leads are the hook, but earnings are why a provider stays. Labels are verbatim from the earnings page, and the figures reconcile — £980.00 paid out + £260.00 available = £1,240.00 earned, at the 10% commission the platform actually charges.
Tradeoff: shows a healthy month to someone who may be having a bad one. Reads as a boast on first launch, when every figure would be zero.
Hand-off frame — the resting beat, shared by both directions (unlike the customer canvas, where A and B rested differently). This is the last thing on screen before the dashboard mounts.

Two things found in the provider app while matching its tokens — flagged, not changed:

1. --muted-foreground is never defined for the provider app. Its globals.css declares --background, --foreground, --surface, --muted and --border in both :root and .dark, but not --muted-foreground — while the compiled CSS still emits .text-muted-foreground{color:hsl(var(--muted-foreground))}. The custom property is invalid at computed-value time, so colour falls back to inherit: 67 provider files' secondary text renders at full foreground weight, with no hierarchy. These artboards use hsl(215 20% 65%), the slate counterpart to what apps/web sets.

2. text-brand-700 has no dark-mode variant. The lead price and the dashboard's links use it; on --surface in dark mode that is 2.1:1, below the 4.5:1 floor. The artboards use brand-300 (#e6975d) instead — 7.8:1 on the same surface.
